extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, visual journalists, editors, and media organizations submitting work to the Pictures of the Year (POY80) competition
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and category-specific criteria for submitting still photos, picture stories, portfolios, video/documentary entries, and editing portfolios to the 80th Pictures of the Year International competition (work from 2022). Includes technical file specs, ethical standards, caption/IPTC requirements, and submission limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1 - Science & Natural History
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that increases the understanding and appreciation of science or the natural world. Studio scenes that are arranged by the photographer are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2 - Science & Natural History Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story, essay, sequence, or series that increases the understanding and appreciation for science or the natural world. Studio scenes that are arranged by the photographer are not eligible. 10 photographs maximum per entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3 - General News
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph of a news event or social issue for which planning was possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4 - Spot News
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph of a breaking news event for which no planning was possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5 - Daily Life
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph, candid and un-posed, that reflects the human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend. Respect for the dignity of the person is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6 - Portrait
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that reflects a strong sense of a person’s identity or narrative. Respect for the dignity of the person is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7 - Portrait Series
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of photographs that reflects a strong sense of identity or narrative. Respect for the dignity of the person is important. 10 photographs maximum per entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8 - National/International News Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story based on daily coverage of general or breaking news that is of primary interest to an entire nation or the world. It is usually created with the intent to share nationally or internationally. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9 - Issue Reporting Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story that explores an important social, economic, or political issue. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10 - Daily Life Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story that reflects the everyday human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend. Respect for the dignity of the person is important. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11 - Local News Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story based on daily coverage of general or breaking news that is of primary interest to the local audience from a media organization or the photographer’s primary geographic market. In other words, a hometown story. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 - War in Ukraine: News
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph of a breaking or general news event related to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13 - War in Ukraine: Daily Life
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph, candid and un-posed, that reflects the perseverance of daily life amid the invasion of Ukraine by Russian forces. Respect for the dignity of the person is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14 - War in Ukraine: Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story based on coverage of events during the invasion of Ukraine by Russian forces. The story could focus on news or daily life. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15 - Sports Action
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that captures peak action of an individual or team sport. Jubilation, dejection, or reaction images should be entered in the Sports Life and Recreational Sports category. Photographs must be taken during 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16 - Sports Life and Recreational Sports
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that celebrates the role sports play in a community. Image may show the emotional highlights of players on the field or the reactions of fans. The sport may be a professional, amateur or intramural competition. Photographs must be taken during 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17 - Sports Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story that increases the understanding of the role that athletics play in the lives of athletes and their community. The story may focus on sports as a catalyst of change in gender, race, political, and cultural issues. It may feature professional or amateur athletes, fans, families, or any aspect of a community that is changed by its relationship to sports. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18 - Documentary News Reporting (video)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single video story based on coverage of general or breaking news. It may be an essay that explores a social, economic, or political issue (flexible length — up to about 15 minutes). Longer stories should be entered in “Documentary Journalism.” Include a thumbnail image and URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not upload video files; submit thumbnail + URL. See Documentary Criteria for additional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19 - Documentary Daily Life (video)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single video story that reflects the human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend. (flexible length — up to about 15 minutes). Longer stories should be entered in “Documentary Journalism.” Include a thumbnail image and URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not upload video files; submit thumbnail + URL. See Documentary Criteria for additional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20 - Documentary Journalism (video)
rubrics_metrics.description: This premiere category recognizes excellence longform Documentary Journalism. This is a single video story the focuses on news, a social issue or cultural trend. Do not enter shorter versions of the same story in other categories. This may be a team entry (approximately 20-45 minutes). Include a thumbnail image and URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not upload video files; submit thumbnail + URL. Longer form; may be team entry. See Documentary Criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21 - Online Storytelling: Daily Life
rubrics_metrics.description: A single story presented on an online platform. It may be based on coverage of an issue, everyday human experience, or a cultural trend. If required, include username and password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide single URL and any required login info when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 22 - Online Storytelling: News Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A single news story presented on an online platform. It may be based on coverage of an issue or daily news. If required, include username and password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide single URL and any required login info when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 23 - Online Storytelling Project of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: This premiere category is open to teams or individuals. It is intended to appraise in-depth visual online journalism that explores a social, economic, or political issue through a special report, series, or presentation with multiple chapters. There is no length limitation. If required, include username and password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple-chaptered projects; if published across multiple platforms choose the platform that best represents the story. Include username/password if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24 - Newspaper Picture Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: A single published story from the coverage of an issue, daily life, or news in a general circulation newspaper. It may include one or more pages from up to 5 consecutive issues. We cannot accept .pdf files. Please convert all .pdf files to .jpg files. Submit each page as a separate .jpg file. A double truck (two facing pages) should be submitted as a single .jpg file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit each page as a separate .jpg; convert PDFs to JPGs; double truck as one JPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: 25 - Magazine Picture Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: A single published story from the coverage of daily life, news or a social issue in a magazine or specialty publication. We cannot accept .pdf files. Please convert all .pdf files to .jpg files. Submit each page as a separate .jpg file. A double truck (two facing pages) should be submitted as a single .jpg file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit each page as a separate .jpg; convert PDFs to JPGs; double truck as one JPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: 26 - Visual Editor of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: This premiere category awards editing excellence to one person. The portfolio should represent the work of an individual who served as the lead editor on a story or package. Newspaper, magazine, and online visual editors may enter. Individual stories may be entered only once and attributed to a single editor. An editing portfolio may consist of content published on multiple platforms; a portfolio entry may present up to 10 stories. The print version of a story may include one or more pages (.jpg files). Please include required usernames and passwords. We cannot accept .pdf files. Submit each page as a separate .jpg file. A double truck should be submitted as a single .jpg file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team entries should enter Angus McDougall Excellence in Editing Award instead. Portfolio may include up to 10 stories; converged print-and-online version counts as one story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 27 - International Photographer of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: This premiere category is open to all photographers — independent, agency, wire service, or newspaper photographers. The work should be of primary interest to a nation or the world, usually created with the intent to share nationally or internationally. Create a title slide (white text, black background) to separate the stories. Fill out the IPTC title and caption fields with the title and description. Place the slide at the start of each story. A portfolio must include at least two narrative picture stories (5 or more images). Single images may be included but are not required. 50 images maximum (not including black slides). Photographers may submit a portfolio into either portfolio category, #27 or #28, but not both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 50 images max; at least two narrative picture stories (5+ images); create IPTC title slide and place at start of each story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 28 - Local Photographer of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: This premiere category is open to all photojournalists. The spirit of this category is to honor a photographer who documents their own community. At least 60% of their portfolio must consist of local or regional coverage from their home or organization’s primary geographic market. Create a title slide (white text, black background) for each story. Fill out IPTC title and caption fields; place the slide at the start of each story. Only one national or international story is allowed. Single images may be included but are not required. A portfolio must include at least two narrative picture stories (5 or more images). 50 photographs maximum (not including the black slides). Photographers may submit a portfolio into either portfolio category, #27 or #28, but not both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least 60% local/regional coverage; only one national/international story allowed; 50 photos max; title slide & IPTC fields required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 - Sports Photographer of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: This premiere category is open to all photographers. A portfolio should include single pictures and at least one narrative picture story. Stories are not limited to 10 images. All single photographs must be taken during 2022. Submit a maximum of 30 photographs. At least three different sports should be represented. Create a title slide (white text, black background) for each story and fill IPTC fields. Entrants may also enter Photographer of the Year category #27 or #28.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-photograph max; at least three different sports; single photos must be from 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30 - Documentary Storyteller of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must have been first published or broadcast during 2022. A portfolio should include 3-5 stories. Each story may have a run time up to about 15 minutes. The portfolio must be the principal work of an individual photojournalist who shot most of the content (video and/or still photographs). Stories may be produced and edited by additional people. A portfolio may be a mix of linear (video) stories and non-linear (user experience) online stories. Entries from the Online Storytelling categories may be included. If required, submit the username and password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 3–5 stories; each up to ~15 minutes; principal work of an individual who shot most content.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 - Environmental Vision Award
rubrics_metrics.description: This premier category recognizes a photographer’s long-term story, project, or essay that explores issues related to the environment, natural history, or science. Submit a maximum of 40 images (a minimum of 12 images). Entries that are comprised primarily of images made in previous years, must have been published for the first time in 2022. Entries need not have been published. If the story has not been published, then at least 60% of the images should have been created in 2022. Winning entries from previous years are not allowed. This is not a category for coverage of human medical issues or natural disasters unless they are a proven result of environmental impact. The project may include a few studio scenes; however, the studio scenes should not make up the majority of images in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 40 images max / 12 min; if unpublished, ≥60% images created in 2022; not for human medical issues or disasters unless proven environmental cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: 32 - Community Awareness Award
rubrics_metrics.description: This Premier category recognizes a photographer’s extended story or essay about the everyday life of the people who make up a community. Submit a maximum of 40 images (a minimum of 12 images). Entries need not have been published. Winning entries from previous years are not allowed. At least 60% of the photos must have been taken during 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 40 images max / 12 min; ≥60% photos taken in 2022; winning previous entries not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 33 - World Understanding Award
rubrics_metrics.description: This Premier category recognizes a photographer’s long-term story, project, or essay that focuses on the human condition and portrays a sense of justice or insight into difficult problems. Submit a maximum of 40 images (a minimum of 12 images). Entries need not have been published. There are no subject requirements. There are no time restrictions. Photos need not have been taken during 2022. Winning entries from previous years may not be resubmitted. Previous World Understanding entries may not be resubmitted for five years. Portions of the essay may not be entered in single or picture story categories. However, portions may be included the Photographer of the Year portfolio entry if the photos were taken or first published in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 40 images max / 12 min; no time restrictions; cannot resubmit World Understanding entries for five years; portions cannot be entered in single/picture story categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: 34 - Angus McDougall Excellence in Editing Award
rubrics_metrics.description: The spirit of this category is to recognize the best in visual editing by a media organization across all platforms. Judges will recognize excellence in use of photojournalism, video, interactive design, user experience, and multimedia storytelling. Only one portfolio entry per organization is allowed. Include up to 10 individual stories. The stories may be a print or online version or a converged print-and-online version of a single topic. All stories must be published in 2022. This category is open to all news organizations, media groups, newspapers, magazines, or specialty advocacy organizations. Personal portfolios, publications or websites are not allowed. Business promotions, catalogs, branded content or stories in which the funding organization is also the primary subject are not allowed. A portfolio may consist of online and print publication stories. Editing should demonstrate sensitivity for the selection and organization of documentary photography. Design should reflect consideration for the reader and respect for the vision of the photographer. The print version of a story may be composed of one or more (.jpg) pages, from no more than five consecutive issues on the coverage of a single topic. The online version of a story may include web pages, apps, mobile-optimized websites, or other platforms. Submit a single URL link for each online story. Make sure the online links are active and the required usernames and passwords are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One portfolio per organization; up to 10 stories; all stories published in 2022; business promotions and personal portfolios not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 - Team Picture Story of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: This premiere category recognizes the collaborative effort of a photography staff covering a single topic or news story. It is a narrative picture story or series that is comprised of images taken as part of a team or staff effort to cover a single issue or news story. Entries are limited to one entry per news organization. 20 images maximum per story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One entry per news organization; 20-image max per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 36 - Photography Book of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: This category recognizes the best documentary visual storytelling in a book. Book entries must rely on documentary photography and have been published within the last three years (2020, 2021, or 2022). Previous entries are not eligible. Photographs may be the work of one or more photographers. The photographer and the publishing house should coordinate to avoid duplicate entries. Submit 1-10 thumbnail images of the book to Picter (include the cover) and mail a physical copy by courier. Include a note with your name and the publisher. Ship the book to POY; shipment need only be postmarked on or before Jan. 18. It is not necessary that the book entry arrive by the contest deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1–10 thumbnails + physical book by courier; books must be published within last 3 years; coordinate to avoid duplicate entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary Criteria (Categories 18, 19, 20, 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term “documentary” is defined as a non-fiction, video narrative, relying on visual evidence to report real situations or events involving real subjects. The photographer should follow the concepts of observational and direct cinema techniques. All documentary entries should adhere to strict journalistic ethics. The content should represent the news, issues, or cultural trends of the past calendar year. Documentaries entered previously are not eligible. Documentaries must be published online or shared publicly via broadcast or festivals during 2022. However, the entry may include content shot in previous years. The entries should be presented in a linear format, edited in a timeline sequence, and presented in a web-based video player. In other words, the viewer clicks "play”, and the story runs from start to finish. Do not upload video files. Not allowed are fictional stories, staged reenactments, docu-dramas, or television news reports where an anchor person tells the story. Stories that feature business promotions, branded content, personal portfolios, or the funding organization as primary subjects are forbidden. For each entry, submit a thumbnail image and a single URL link. Make sure the links are active. If password access is required, please include a password and username.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linear, play-to-completion video format in web player; thumbnail + active URL required; no uploads; no staged or fictional content; must be publicly shared/published in 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Storytelling Criteria (Categories 21, 22, 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent of these categories is to recognize excellent visual editing in multiple-chaptered stories or projects on an online platform, primarily websites. Open to all — teams or individuals, either independent or affiliated with media organizations. Projects must have been either shot, produced, or published for the first time in 2022. Portfolios, business promotions, agency catalogs, or personal websites are not eligible. Also, not eligible are stories that include the funding organization as the primary subject. If a story is published across multiple platforms, choose the one platform that best represents that specific story. Updated versions of the originally posted story are acceptable. For websites, provide a single URL link to the relevant page along with the required usernames and passwords. Web pages that present only a single video should be submitted in the documentary categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-chapter online projects; first shot/produced/published in 2022; select one representative platform; include URL + login details if required; single-video pages go to documentary categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture Editing Criteria (Categories 24, 25, 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: These categories are intended to appraise visual storytelling in the printed pages through the effective use of photojournalism, captions, headlines, and other display typography. Entries include the print version of a single story and may include up to five consecutive issues. Open to all — teams or individuals, either independent or affiliated with media organizations. Portfolios, business promotions, catalogs, or personal publications are not eligible. Also, not eligible are stories that include the funding organization as the primary subject or narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated on visual storytelling, selection and organization of photos, captions, headlines and typography; convert PDFs to JPGs and submit pages accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: A maximum of 15 submissions allowed per person
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum of 15 submissions can be entered in any combination of categories. A single submission is one entry, one project or one portfolio. It is defined as: One picture in a single-picture category. One picture story (5-10 photographs). One project (12-40 photographs) in the premiere categories (10-20 images for cat. 34). One portfolio in the Angus McDougal Excellence in Editing, Documentary Storyteller, Photographer or Visual Editor of the Year categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count carefully: picture = 1; picture story 5–10 = 1 entry; project/portfolio definitions vary by category (see above).

rubrics_metrics.name: File Specifications (type, size, resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: File type: .JPG. Image Size: 3,000 pixels minimum on the longer side. Resolution: 300 dpi, minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files are automatically renamed on submit; no need for manual renaming. Print editing entries must be JPG (convert PDFs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture Captions / IPTC metadata requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each photograph must include a caption embedded in the .jpg file's IPTC metadata description field that meets journalistic standards for accuracy and ready-for-publication requirements. Required IPTC fields: Document Title is the image title; Author is the photographer's name; Description is the caption; Location Information include city (or nearest city), state/province, country; Capture Date verify the date. Each caption should include a date, or an approximation of the date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include your name in the caption. Examples of acceptable date formats provided (e.g., 'The photo was taken on Feb. 4, 2022' or 'in February 2022'). Use Photoshop, Photo Mechanic, Lightroom, Bridge or other tools to embed IPTC. Picter will display the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture Submissions rules and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph may be submitted only once among the single-picture categories. A single photograph may be entered as a single photograph and included as part of one picture story. A picture story consists of 5–10 photos and counts as one entry. Do not re-edit photos from the same story and then submit it as a different story. Images submitted into single-photo categories cannot be copies, scans, or a photograph of other photographs or documents. A photograph of a photograph can serve as a detail image in a larger picture story or project, but they may not comprise a majority of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges often review category rules; entries should be in the correct category because judges cannot move entries. Picture Story entries should have a clearly defined structure; eliminate weak and redundant images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio Submission rules (title slides, captions, timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: For portfolio categories, create a title slide (white text on black background). It is important to include the story title and story description in the IPTC document title and caption fields of the slide. Place the slide at the beginning of each story. Picture stories in portfolios are not limited to 10 images. All photographs must include captions. The majority of photos in the portfolio must have been taken during 2022 or the entire project must have been first published in 2022 (Exception: World Understanding Award has no time restrictions). Single images within a portfolio should not be repeated in a picture story in the same portfolio. POY staff will not separate a portfolio and enter the images into individual categories. If you want to enter work from your portfolio into single or picture story categories, you must upload separate entries into those categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title slide provides important context—keep it short. POY staff will not separate portfolio items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyrights & Usage Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: By entering this competition, you declare that you meet the eligibility requirements and that you are authorized by the holder of the copyright to submit photos and multimedia entries. You grant permission to Pictures of the Year International, the Reynolds Journalism Institute and the Missouri School of Journalism and POY programs to use your submitted material in exhibitions, publications, in promotion of the competition itself, and for educational research and historical record purposes concerning POY. This usage includes print, electronic and online platforms; entries may become part of the permanent POY archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you are authorized by the copyright holder to submit and grant POY the listed usage rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fee / educational mission note
rubrics_metrics.description: POY provides an educational mission and requests $50 (U.S. dollars) compensation from participants to cover costs associated with operation of the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing / manipulation and authenticity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must not be digitally manipulated or altered through post-production processing. Routine post-production processing of images for exposure correction, white balance and color toning is acceptable. Adding, altering, or removing elements is not permitted. Excessive saturation or desaturation is also not allowed. Heavily edited images turn off judges. Color images should replicate what the human eye experiences. Flagrant pre- or post-production effects that use excessive tonal aberrations, textures, vignettes, color saturation or other manipulations may be disqualified. Diptychs and triptychs are not eligible. Digitally manufactured photo illustrations, double exposures, in-camera multiple exposures, added masks, borders, backgrounds, text, handwritten notes, or other artistic effects are all prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine corrections okay; do not add/remove elements; avoid excessive artistic/creative filters and effects; diptychs/triptychs and manufactured illustrations are disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black & white image requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Black & white images should be bi-tonal and display a full grayscale range of 256 intensities from black to white. Black & white image files that artificially impose a color shift, such as sepia or cyan tones, may be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B/W must be true grayscale; artificial color shifts are grounds for disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smartphone photo eligibility and filter restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Photos from smartphone cameras are eligible. However, the use of software capture filters that apply excessive tonal aberrations, textures, vignettes, or other artistic manipulations will be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smartphone images allowed, but avoid built-in filters or apps that create heavy artistic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diptychs/triptychs and artificial effects prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Diptychs and triptychs are not eligible. Digitally manufactured photo illustrations, double exposures, in-camera multiple exposures, added masks, borders, backgrounds, text, handwritten notes, or other artistic effects are all prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: All still-photography entries must be by a single photographer
rubrics_metrics.description: All photographs entered in the still photography categories must be taken by a single photographer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video and URL entry technical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a thumbnail image and a single URL via an active link. Do not upload video files. Include required usernames and passwords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure URL is active and provide login credentials if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required IPTC fields (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required IPTC fields: Document Title (image title), Author (photographer's name), Description (caption), Location Information (city or nearest city, state/province, country), Capture Date (verify the date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify capture dates; incorrect dates may make images ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: POY pre-judging review and RAW file verification
rubrics_metrics.description: POY staff reviews every entry in advance of judging. POY will request the original RAW or JPG image files from a random selection of photographs voted to final places by the jury, plus any images that the jury members or POY staff request. POY will examine and verify each of these selected files for authenticity. Any photographs that do not meet these standards will be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep original RAW/JPG originals available for potential submission; failure to provide authentic originals may lead to disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture story editing and sequence preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: The order or sequence of images you create will be preserved. You can change the sequence after you upload the images. POY staff cannot change the order of the pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit story sequence carefully prior to finalizing uploads because staff will not change order once set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' discretion and disqualification authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Once judging begins, judges have the discretion to disqualify entries that they think over manipulate the image. POY staff will contact photographers whose images seem to conflict with these standards and provide them with the opportunity to resubmit the photograph before judging begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contacted, you may be allowed a resubmission before judging starts; judges have final discretion during judging rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption importance and judging focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions are read in the final rounds of each category. Well-written captions with relevant details strengthen your entry and stand apart from entries with weak captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate, publication-ready captions; judges often focus on the quality of the edit and the caption in final rounds.
